newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela's imports up 37 pct in first quarter.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela's imports up 37 pct in first quarter.

text.p: The value of Venezuela's imports rose by $642 million, or 36.7 percent, in the first three months of 1997 to $2.390 billion, compared to 1.748 billion in the first quarter of 1996, according to the Central Office of Statistics and Information (OCEI).
Imports in the month of March, at $846 million, were up $190 million, or 29 percent from $656 billion in March 1996, the OCEI said in a release.
The private sector accounted for the vast majority of imports in the first quarter of 1997 with 86 percent of the total.
"Electrical materials" was the biggest category of imports with 30.0 percent of the total. "Chemical products" followed with 12.2 percent and "common metals" with 10.9 percent.

The United States was the top exporter to Venezuela, accounting for 44.9 percent of the total, followed by Colombia with 7.9 percent, Germany with 4.5 percent, Brazil with 3.9 percent, Japan with 2.8 percent and Italy with 2.8 percent.
